content.comment_body: Hello everyone. Is it possible with the [product_name] [article_no] to have a real time clock feature with automatic time correction, and can Q output be activated every minute automatically? Thank you.
Could you specify which exact [product_name] [article_no] you have? Please provide the full article number and firmware version.

The answer is partly yes. The [product_name] [article_no] includes a real time clock, but you must set the time manually when powering it up for the first time. It has a backup battery; if power is lost for a period longer than the battery can support (about 20 days when fully charged), you'll need to reset the time manually. The clock is not synchronized externally, and can deviate by around 2 seconds per day. It does support automatic summer/winter time changes, which you can configure for different regions or manually by date. The smallest interval for switching ON or OFF is 1 minute. You can connect it to an extension unit ([product_name] for communication), which can synchronize the time using GPS and then transfer it to the [product_name], allowing the time to be synced.

This feature is not available on all [product_name] [article_no] modules, only on the [product_name] 8.0 ([article_no], Standard). Starting with [product_name] 8.1 and firmware [version_no], time and date can be synchronized via a network time protocol (NTP) server. Devices with earlier firmware can be updated to [version_no] through a firmware update. I personally use [product_name] 8.2 and 8.3, with my router acting as the NTP server. That's why I asked which [product_name] version and firmware you are using.
Actually, that's not accurate. The [product_name] CSM module is an unmanaged 4-port switch. Only the CMR module can handle synchronizing date and time for your [product_name] [article_no].

Hello, Nowadays, nearly all internet routers include an NTP server. If you connect a [product_name] 8.2 or 8.3 to such a router, you can use its NTP server for synchronizing date and time. If your [product_name] is installed in an area without internet access, you can use either the CMR or CIM modules, which can connect to an NTP server via mobile network providers. Hope this clarifies things.
Thank you all for your assistance.
You are correct, I mentioned the wrong version numbers earlier.

Additionally, it's possible to transmit the time signal via a separate NTP server using GPS, Galileo, or long-wave signals. For those who enjoy working on solutions themselves, building a custom NTP server with a Raspberry Pi that receives long-wave signals is also an option.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants discussed the real time clock capabilities of the [product_name] [article_no], clarifying distinctions in time synchronization features across different versions. Earlier [product_name] modules require manual time setup due to their independent RTC operation and limited battery backup. More recent models and firmware versions add NTP synchronization, boosting accuracy and reducing the need for manual adjustments. The conversation also highlighted confusion regarding which modules and extensions support automated time correction, underlining the importance of knowing your exact model and firmware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] [article_no] to precisely and automatically handle timekeeping and enable minute-based Q output activation, without requiring manual time correction.
